title: input: select what a Helix word motion moves over, as Helix does
body:
The Helix keymap of a copy mode built `w`, `e` and `b` from `collapse_selection` and `extend_selection`. That kept the old head cell in the new selection, so a `b` from the start of a word selected one cell too many, and a `w` walked to the end of the row when the next word was on the next row.

Now `select_word:<next|end|prev>` is the `range_to_target` of Helix (`helix-core/src/movement.rs`) over cells: the anchor steps off the cursor when the cursor is already on a boundary, line ends after the cursor are skipped and left out, and the head stops where the cursor of Helix stops. The word motions of `move_selection` and `extend_selection` take their head from the same walk, so a select-mode `w` lands where a normal-mode `w` does. The cells after the last text of a row are a line end, so a cursor that a click put there walks on as a cursor on a newline does in Helix.

The Helix mode of Zed (`crates/vim/src/helix.rs`) was the second reference: its tests have `w` stop on the last character of the last word of a line and `b` from a word start select the blanks before it, and its select mode keeps the anchor and uses the cursor of the normal motion.

Patch 0017 in the downstream delta. The tests are `Selection: selectWord ...` and `parse: select_word`, which the build's filters run.
